evidence.quote: South Lyon City Council this week adopted a 12-month moratorium on new data center applications -- extending it beyond the original proposal of six months to match a similar pause recently enacted in Northville.

legal_basis.from: Resolution 2025-11, Temporary Moratorium on Approval of Data Centers
legal_basis.to: Resolution 2025-11 (adopted Dec. 11, 2025; 180-day term, ~expiring June 9, 2026). Before that term lapsed, the Township Board extended it twice: a 30-day extension on May 14, 2026 (pushing the expiration to July 9, 2026), and again on July 9, 2026 via Resolution 2026-09, which amends Resolution 2025-11 and extends the moratorium through December 10, 2026.
legal_basis.reason: The Township's own July 9, 2026 board meeting minutes (archived PDF) document the adoption of Resolution 2026-09 extending the moratorium to Dec. 10, 2026, and okoenv.com's sourced timeline (citing the May 14, 2026 board minutes) documents the earlier 30-day extension to July 9, 2026.

current_status.from: Expired approximately 2026-06-09 at the end of the documented 180-day term. No adopted extension was located through 2026-08-19. [VERIFY: post-expiry Township action not located]
current_status.to: Active as of 2026-09-23. The Township Board extended the moratorium twice before it could lapse: a 30-day extension adopted May 14, 2026 (to July 9, 2026), and Resolution 2026-09, adopted July 9, 2026, extending it through December 10, 2026. As of Sept. 22, 2026, the Planning Commission and a newly formed data-center zoning sub-committee (formed Sept. 10, 2026) were still reviewing a Carlisle/Wortman draft ordinance and had not finalized permanent regulations, so the moratorium remains in force. Separately, the property owner at the original 84-acre Andersonville Road site of interest confirmed on Aug. 26, 2026 that a data center will not be built there; that owner is instead pursuing a storage/office development.
current_status.reason: Directly resolves the post-expiry VERIFY marker: the Township did not allow the moratorium to lapse, but extended it twice, most recently through Dec. 10, 2026, which is confirmed by the Township's own board meeting minutes (a primary source).

duration.to: 180 days as originally adopted (Dec. 11, 2025 - ~Jun. 9, 2026); extended 30 days (to Jul. 9, 2026) by board action May 14, 2026; extended again through Dec. 10, 2026 by Resolution 2026-09, adopted Jul. 9, 2026.
duration.reason: Documents the full extension history found this pass.

current_end_date_iso.reason: Per the Township's July 9, 2026 board meeting minutes: 'Resolution 2026-09 amends the original resolution and extends the current moratorium through December 10, 2026.'

verify_resolutions.marker: [VERIFY: post-expiry Township action not located]

The moratorium was never allowed to lapse.

legal_basis.from: Township moratorium [VERIFY: ordinance/resolution number not posted on Sylvan Township website as of 2026-04-29]
legal_basis.to: Ordinance 26-01 (also referenced as 26-001), adopted Jan. 13, 2026, effective Jan. 28, 2026: a 180-day moratorium on accepting/processing data-center applications only. Before that term lapsed, the Township Board adopted Resolution 26-05 at its July 14, 2026 regular meeting, imposing a new 12-month moratorium on data centers, high-energy users, power-generation facilities, and similar uses (excluding PA 233 of 2023 energy facilities and small-scale generators), effective immediately.
legal_basis.reason: The Sun Times News published Sylvan Township's own statutory notices of adoption for both instruments (Ordinance 26-01 on Jan. 13, 2026, and Resolution 26-05 on July 14, 2026), resolving both the missing-instrument-number marker and clarifying that a broader successor moratorium replaced the original before it expired.

current_status.from: Expired approximately 2026-07-21 at the end of the limited 180-day term, absent a documented earlier replacement ordinance or extension. [VERIFY: post-expiry Township action not located]
current_status.to: Active as of 2026-09-23. Resolution 26-05, adopted July 14, 2026 (effective immediately), imposes a 12-month moratorium on data centers, high-energy users, power-generation facilities, and similar uses, running through approximately July 14, 2027. This resolution was adopted before the original Ordinance 26-01's 180-day term (effective Jan. 28, 2026) would have lapsed around late July 2026, so the Township's data-center pause continued without a gap. The Township Board may extend Resolution 26-05 in increments of up to six months if more time is needed.
current_status.reason: Resolves the post-expiry VERIFY marker: rather than letting the moratorium lapse, the Township adopted a new, broader-scope, longer-duration resolution shortly before the original ordinance's term would have ended.

duration.to: 180 days under the original Ordinance 26-01 (effective Jan. 28, 2026); superseded before expiry by a 12-month term under Resolution 26-05 (effective July 14, 2026), extendable by the Township Board in increments of up to six months.

duration_days.reason: The currently operative instrument (Resolution 26-05, adopted July 14, 2026) sets a 12-month (365-day) term, superseding the original 180-day Ordinance 26-01.
